findings.evidence: Line 271 exposes `Submodule.span ℤ (Set.range (basis ℚ n))`; lines 277–315 provide membership, coordinate, and rank characterizations, and no `attribute [irreducible] integralLattice` exists.
findings.fix: Remove `@[expose]`, or mark the definition `irreducible` after the last proof that genuinely needs unfolding and use the public membership/spanning lemmas thereafter.
findings.issue: `integralLattice` is `@[expose]` despite `mem_integralLattice_iff`, the coordinate equivalence, and spanning/rank lemmas providing its characteristic API; its span-of-basis body remains available downstream.

findings.evidence: Line 470 adds `@[expose]`; lines 505–512 supply the simp-normal action theorem, and no irreducibility barrier follows it.
findings.fix: Hide the body after establishing the application theorem, using an opaque proof such as `:= (rfl)` where needed rather than leaving downstream unfolding available.
findings.issue: `kostantRepresentationIntegralLattice` exposes its entire structure literal although `coe_kostantRepresentationIntegralLattice_apply` already characterizes its action.

findings.evidence: Line 359 exposes the `Pi.basisFun` body; lines 365–375 provide the basis, representation-coordinate, and evaluation equations, with no `attribute [irreducible] basis`.
findings.fix: Keep `basis` unexposed, or make it irreducible immediately after its characteristic lemmas so consumers use those lemmas instead of unfolding to `Pi.basisFun`.
findings.issue: The PR newly exposes `basis` even though `basis_eq`, `basis_repr_apply`, and `basis_apply` completely describe the coordinate basis.

summary: Three fully characterized definitions are unnecessarily exposed, allowing downstream proofs to depend on implementation details instead of the supplied API.
